name: Full vs partial map by task
keywords: layout; full map; side panel; exploration; workflow; task
do: Use a full-map layout for exploration and a map plus side panel for task-funneled workflows.
dont: Do not default to one layout without thinking about the user task.
why: The layout should follow what users do: browse freely or move through a guided sequence.
checklist: Was the layout (full map vs map plus panel) chosen from the main user task?

name: Primary panel on the reading-start side
keywords: panel; left; rtl; ltr; reading order; sidebar
do: Put the primary panel on the reading-start side: left for LTR languages, mirrored for RTL.
dont: Do not put the main panel on the far side from where users start reading.
why: Users scan from the reading-start edge, so the primary tools are found first.

name: Shell layout with action bar
keywords: shell; header; action bar; icon rail; collapsible panel; calcite
do: Use a header, an action bar (icon rail) that opens collapsible panels, and the map in the content area.
dont: Do not stack always-open widgets over the map.
why: A shell keeps the map area large and tools discoverable on demand.
checklist: Do tools live in a header plus action bar with collapsible panels instead of always-open widgets on the map?

name: Action bar overflow
keywords: action bar; overflow; more menu; short screen; adaptive; clipped
do: Collapse the action bar into a 'more' menu when the screen is short.
dont: Do not clip tools silently when the viewport height shrinks.
why: Tools that disappear without a trace cannot be found or used on small or short screens.

name: Size elements by importance
keywords: size; hierarchy; kpi; map largest; dashboard; uniform grid; importance
do: Make the most critical element (the map or the headline KPI) the largest on the page.
dont: Do not use a uniform tile grid where every element has the same weight.
why: Visual size signals priority and speeds up reading of a dashboard.
checklist: Is the most important element (map or headline KPI) visibly the largest?

name: Group related elements
keywords: group; proximity; legend near map; details next to list; related
do: Keep the legend next to the map and the details next to the list they describe.
dont: Do not scatter related elements across the page.
why: Proximity tells users which elements belong together and cuts eye travel.
checklist: Are related elements (legend and map, list and details) placed together?

name: Audience and display target first
keywords: audience; display; wall screen; laptop; kiosk; test device; target
do: Define the audience and the display target first, then test on the real display (a wall screen vs a laptop).
dont: Do not design on a laptop only and assume it works on a wall display or projector.
why: Font size, density and interaction needs differ between a control-room wall and a personal device.
checklist: Was the layout tested on the real target display for the intended audience?

name: Only what users need
keywords: minimal; clutter; nice-to-have; charts; focus; slow
do: Include only what users need to answer their questions and leave out nice-to-have charts.
dont: Do not add widgets just because the data allows it.
why: Clutter hides the key message and also slows the app down.
checklist: Does every element on the page answer a user question (no nice-to-have clutter)?

name: Mobile layout: map on top, bottom sheet
keywords: mobile; bottom sheet; responsive; 768px; touch; phone; small screen; map
do: Below 768px put the map on top (about 70vh) and a bottom sheet (30vh or less) underneath, with touch-sized controls.
dont: Do not squeeze a side panel next to the map on a phone.
why: A narrow viewport has no room for side-by-side panes; stacking keeps the map usable and the details reachable.
checklist: Below 768px is the map on top with a bottom sheet instead of a side panel?
code_bad: #panel{position:absolute;left:0;width:320px}  /* covers the map on a 375px phone */

name: Short title and an about panel
keywords: title; about; purpose; data description; intro; help
do: Use a short title and an about panel that briefly explains the app purpose and data.
dont: Do not leave users guessing what the map shows or where the data came from.
why: A brief explanation sets context for first-time users.

name: Z-order of map and UI layers
keywords: z-order; stacking; overlap; attribution uncovered; panels; popups; toast
do: Stack bottom to top: basemap, thematic, reference labels/boundaries, selection highlight, controls, panels, popups, modals/toasts. Keep attribution uncovered.
dont: Do not let panels, legends or toasts cover the attribution or the selection highlight.
why: A fixed stacking order avoids hidden controls and legal attribution problems.
checklist: Does the stacking order follow basemap, thematic, reference, highlight, controls, panels, popups, modals, with attribution uncovered?

name: Map-first vs data-first
keywords: map-first; list-first; lookup; where; store locator; sorted by distance
do: Use map-first when the question is 'where?'. Use list-first for lookup tasks, sorted by distance or time.
dont: Do not force a map when users really need to find one item in a list.
why: The primary question decides which view should lead.

name: Attribution always visible
keywords: attribution; visible; osm; copyright; collapse; license; credit
do: Make attribution visible without interaction. It may collapse after being shown (dismiss, map interaction or after about 5 s) but must stay findable, for example via an (i) button. Any corner is fine; lower right is traditional.
dont: Do not hide attribution behind an 'i' on load.
why: Attribution is a licence requirement; OSMF says it must not require interaction to see and startup-only display is enough.
checklist: Is attribution visible on load without any interaction, and findable after it collapses?
code_good: new mapboxgl.Map({container:'map', attributionControl:true}); // default visible control
code_bad: new mapboxgl.Map({container:'map', attributionControl:false}); // and nothing re-adds it

name: Mapbox logo and text attribution
keywords: mapbox; logo; attribution; hidden; text; wordmark; display none; required
do: Keep both the Mapbox logo and the attribution text on the map (typically logo bottom-left; GL JS places the text bottom-right by default). The logo may be moved but not restyled.
dont: Do not hide, crop or restyle the logo or text, for example with CSS display:none.
why: Both are required by the Mapbox terms.
checklist: Are both the Mapbox logo and attribution text visible and unmodified?

name: Attribution in Leaflet and OpenLayers
keywords: leaflet; openlayers; attribution; manual; mapbox tiles; raster tiles; credit
do: Add attribution manually when using Mapbox tiles in Leaflet or OpenLayers.
dont: Do not assume these libraries add Mapbox attribution automatically.
why: They may not automatically add the necessary attribution.
checklist: When using Leaflet or OpenLayers, is the tile provider attribution added explicitly?

name: Control corner conventions
keywords: controls; corners; top-right; zoom; compass; scale bar; search; position
do: Stack zoom, compass, geolocate and fullscreen top-right, scale bar bottom-left, attribution at the bottom, search top-left or in the header.
dont: Do not scatter controls at random corners or let them overlap attribution.
why: Consistent positions match what users learned from other web maps.
checklist: Do controls follow corner conventions (nav top-right, scale bottom-left, attribution bottom)?

name: Compass only if the map can rotate
keywords: compass; rotate; bearing; north; reset north
do: Show the compass only if the map can rotate; clicking it resets to north.
dont: Do not show a compass on a north-locked map.
why: A control that does nothing adds clutter.

name: Scale bar with locale units
keywords: scale bar; metric; imperial; units; locale; ratio; 1:50000
do: Use metric or imperial to match the locale; offer a toggle where users mix both.
dont: Never show a fixed ratio such as 1:50,000 on a web map.
why: Screen size and DPI vary, so a printed-style ratio is wrong on the web.

name: Geolocate states and permission
keywords: geolocate; location; permission; tracking; error; locating; gps
do: Show off, locating, tracking and error states. Ask for permission on tap, not on page load.
dont: Do not trigger the browser permission prompt on page load.
why: An unexpected prompt is usually denied and erodes trust.

name: Keyboard shortcuts help
keywords: keyboard; shortcuts; help; focus order; arrow keys; control
do: Provide a keyboard shortcuts help control placed before the map in focus order.
dont: Do not rely on users guessing the map keyboard shortcuts.
why: Keyboard users need to discover how to pan, zoom and select.

name: Search or coordinate input as drag alternative
keywords: search; coordinates; drag alternative; pan; geocoder; wcag 2.5.7; input
do: Provide search or coordinate input so the view can be set without dragging.
dont: Do not make dragging the only way to reach a location.
why: WCAG 2.5.7 (AA) requires a single-pointer alternative to dragging.
checklist: Can users reach any location by search or coordinate entry, without dragging the map?

name: Measure and draw tools
keywords: measure; draw; area; length; editable; export; geometry; polygon
do: Show area and length live while drawing; keep geometry editable and exportable.
dont: Do not make users draw once and lose the geometry or the value.
why: Measurement and AOI drawing are core tasks and need to be reusable.

name: Basemap switcher
keywords: basemap; switcher; thumbnails; satellite; dark; contrast; style
do: Offer 2 to 4 basemap thumbnails and re-check overlay contrast on each basemap.
dont: Do not offer many basemaps or leave overlays unreadable on some of them.
why: Overlay colors that work on a light basemap can vanish on imagery or dark styles.
code_bad: map.setStyle(url); addOverlays(); // layers lost when style reloads

name: Only purposeful layers
keywords: layers; default off; purposeful; clutter; visibility; toggle
do: Include only purposeful layers and turn non-essential layers off by default.
dont: Do not switch every available layer on at load.
why: Too many visible layers hide the message and slow rendering.
checklist: Are non-essential layers off by default?
code_bad: map.addLayer({id:'parcels', type:'line', source:'p'}); // always on, no toggle

name: Min/max visible scale on every layer
keywords: min zoom; max zoom; scale; visibility range; minzoom; maxzoom; scale dependency
do: Set minimum and maximum visible scale (minzoom/maxzoom) on every layer.
dont: Do not draw detailed layers at world zoom or coarse layers at street zoom.
why: Scale ranges keep the map legible and cut draw cost.
checklist: Does every layer have a min/max visible zoom range?
code_bad: map.addLayer({id:'buildings', type:'fill', source:'b'}); // 10M polygons at zoom 2

name: Grey out layers outside visible scale
keywords: grey out; out of scale; zoom to visible; disabled layer; layer list
do: Grey out layers whose zoom range excludes the current view and offer 'zoom to visible'.
dont: Do not leave a checked layer that silently draws nothing.
why: Users otherwise think the layer is broken.

name: Human-readable titles and field aliases
keywords: title; alias; field name; objectid; coded values; labels; readable
do: Use human-readable layer titles and field aliases; hide OBJECTID and coded values.
dont: Do not expose raw field names like OBJECTID or code 3.
why: Plain labels are readable by non-GIS audiences.
checklist: Are layer titles and field names human-readable, with IDs and codes hidden?

name: Layer order
keywords: layer order; basemap; thematic; reference; labels on top; raster under vector; beforeId
do: Order bottom to top: basemap, thematic, reference lines and labels. Put raster under vector.
dont: Do not draw a raster over vector or labels, or boundaries under a fill.
why: Wrong order hides labels and boundaries.
checklist: Are rasters under vectors and reference labels on top?

name: Per-layer opacity slider
keywords: opacity; transparency; slider; raster; blend; layer control
do: Offer a per-layer opacity slider, especially for rasters.
dont: Do not force users to choose between fully opaque and off.
why: Opacity lets users compare imagery with the basemap beneath.

name: Grouping layers
keywords: groups; collapsible; radio; mutually exclusive; checkboxes; layer list; theme
do: Use collapsible theme groups. Mutually exclusive rasters use radio buttons. Avoid a flat list of more than 15 checkboxes.
dont: Do not allow two opaque rasters on at once.
why: Grouping keeps long layer lists scannable and prevents stacked opaque rasters.

name: Normalize choropleths
keywords: choropleth; normalize; rate; raw counts; density; per capita; area size bias
do: Map rates or densities (per capita, per km2).
dont: Never map raw counts in a choropleth.
why: Large areas look important simply because they are large or populous.
checklist: Does every choropleth show a normalized rate rather than raw counts?

name: Totals as proportional symbols or dot density
keywords: proportional symbols; totals; dot density; counts; circle size; absolute
do: Show totals and counts with proportional symbols or dot density.
dont: Do not show totals through area fills.
why: Symbol size encodes magnitude without being tied to polygon area.
checklist: Are absolute totals shown with proportional symbols or dots rather than fills?

name: Dot density needs an equal-area projection
keywords: dot density; equal area; projection; mercator; distortion; dots
do: Use an equal-area projection for dot density maps.
dont: Do not place dots on Web Mercator across large latitude ranges.
why: Mercator inflates polar areas so dot density looks falsely sparse or dense.
checklist: Is a dot density map drawn in an equal-area projection?

name: Number of classes
keywords: classes; class count; breaks; bins; legend; sequential; diverging; qualitative; number
do: Use 3 to 7 classes for sequential ramps (CARTO ramps stop at 7; ColorBrewer sequential goes up to 9), at most 11 for diverging, and about 8 or fewer for qualitative (some schemes such as Paired and Set3 go to 12; Set2 only to 8).
dont: Do not use more classes than readers can tell apart.
why: Too many classes make legend colors indistinguishable.
checklist: Is the number of classes within the limit for the ramp type?

name: Classification method
keywords: classification; jenks; quantile; equal interval; fixed breaks; natural breaks; compare
do: Jenks for clustered data on a single map; quantile for rankings or evenly spread data; equal interval for familiar ranges; fixed breaks when maps must be compared.
dont: Do not use per-map automatic breaks when maps are compared side by side.
why: The method changes the story the map tells.
checklist: Was the classification method chosen deliberately (fixed breaks when maps are compared)?

name: Ramp type matches the data
keywords: ramp; sequential; diverging; qualitative; midpoint; categories; palette type
do: Sequential for ordered values; diverging only with a meaningful midpoint; qualitative for categories.
dont: Do not use a diverging ramp without a real midpoint or a sequential one for categories.
why: The ramp type signals the data structure.
checklist: Does the ramp type (sequential, diverging, qualitative) match the data?

name: Lightness direction follows the basemap
keywords: lightness; dark basemap; light basemap; high value; dark mode; ramp direction
do: On a light basemap dark means high; on a dark basemap bright means high.
dont: Do not reuse the same ramp direction on both basemaps.
why: High values must stand out from the background.
checklist: Does the ramp lightness direction match the basemap (dark=high on light, bright=high on dark)?

name: No rainbow or jet ramps
keywords: rainbow; jet; color ramp; continuous; perceptual; viridis; spectrum
do: Use perceptually ordered ramps (viridis-like, single-hue sequential) for continuous data.
dont: Do not use rainbow or jet color ramps for continuous data.
why: Rainbow has false boundaries and uneven lightness, which distorts the data and fails for color-vision deficiency.
checklist: Are continuous fields free of rainbow or jet ramps?

name: Colorblind-safe palettes
keywords: colorblind; cvd; accessible palette; red green; colorbrewer; safe; deuteranopia
do: Use ColorBrewer colorblind-safe schemes (YlGnBu, YlOrRd, Blues, Greens, RdBu, BrBG, PuOr) or CARTO Safe. Check Set2 only for 3 classes.
dont: Never encode meaning with red and green alone.
why: About 1 in 12 men have a color-vision deficiency.
checklist: Is the palette colorblind-safe, with no red-green-only encoding?

name: Muted basemap, strong data
keywords: basemap; muted; contrast; data stands out; grayscale; subdued; background
do: Mute the basemap (low saturation, light or dark gray) so the data layer is the strongest element.
dont: Do not put saturated thematic colors on a busy basemap.
why: Data should be the visual focus of a data map.
checklist: Is the basemap muted enough for the data layer to dominate?

name: Reveal detail progressively by zoom
keywords: progressive; detail; zoom; generalize; labels; level of detail
do: Show coarse features at low zoom and add detail and labels as users zoom in.
dont: Do not show all detail at every zoom.
why: Progressive detail keeps maps legible at every scale.

name: Use color only for data differences
keywords: color; meaning; decorative; consistent; semantic; encode
do: Use color only to encode data differences, and use the same color for the same meaning everywhere.
dont: Do not use color decoratively or give one color two meanings.
why: Color is the strongest visual variable; spent on decoration it hides data.

name: Minimal legend
keywords: legend; minimal; single column; units; hidden layers; direct labels
do: Single column for a ramp, units labeled, no entries for hidden layers; drop the legend if direct labels are enough.
dont: Do not list every layer or show legend entries for hidden layers.
why: A clean legend gets read.

name: Legend reflects what is drawn
keywords: legend; dynamic; visible layers; filter; in scale; sync; update
do: Show only visible, in-scale layers and reflect the current filter.
dont: Do not keep a static legend that disagrees with the map.
why: A mismatched legend misleads readers.

name: Heatmap vs choropleth
keywords: heatmap; intensity; density; choropleth; rate per unit; values
do: Use heatmaps for event intensity and choropleths for rates per unit.
dont: Never ask users to read exact values off a heatmap.
why: Heatmap color depends on zoom and radius and carries no precise values.

name: Cluster dense points at low zoom
keywords: cluster; dense points; clusterMaxZoom; count; overplotting; points
do: Cluster dense points at low zoom; show a count and set clusterMaxZoom.
dont: Do not draw tens of thousands of overlapping point symbols.
why: Clustering removes overplotting and cuts rendering cost.
checklist: Are dense point layers clustered at low zoom, with clusterMaxZoom set?

name: Cluster popups summarize
keywords: cluster popup; summary; count; dominant category; zoom to; browse
do: Show the count, the dominant category and browse or zoom-to actions in a cluster popup.
dont: Do not open a popup listing every member of a large cluster.
why: A summary lets users decide whether to drill in.

name: No-data gets its own legend class
keywords: no data; nodata; no clear image; missing; not observed; cloud masked; legend class; unknown; grey
do: Give no-data or not-observed its own legend class (neutral grey, hatch or outline), distinct from "normal" and from zero.
dont: Do not paint missing, cloud-masked or not-observed features in the "normal" class.
why: A missing measurement read as normal hides exactly the places where nothing is known.
checklist: Does the legend have a class for no data that is separate from normal and from zero?

name: Roth interaction operators
keywords: interaction; operators; pan; zoom; filter; search; retrieve; overlay; resymbolize; sequence
do: Check the design against Roth's operators: pan, zoom, filter, search, retrieve, overlay, resymbolize, reexpress, sequence, arrange, calculate, reproject.
dont: Do not ship only pan and zoom when users need to filter, search and retrieve.
why: A taxonomy of interaction primitives shows which user tasks have no support.

name: Hover highlights, click opens details
keywords: hover; highlight; popup; click; feature-state; cursor; details
do: On hover change feature-state and the cursor; open the full popup only on click.
dont: Do not open a big popup on hover.
why: Hover popups flicker and are unusable on touch devices.
checklist: Does hover only highlight (feature-state, cursor) while click opens the details?

name: Clear the previous highlight
keywords: highlight; clear; mouseleave; feature-state; reset; previous
do: Clear the previous highlight on mouseleave or when a new feature is selected.
dont: Do not leave stale highlighted features behind.
why: Stale highlights suggest more than one active selection.

name: Curated popup fields
keywords: popup; fields; alias; formatted; title first; attributes; curated
do: Show curated fields with aliases and formatted values, title first.
dont: Never dump every attribute into the popup.
why: Popups are for quick reading, not data export.
checklist: Do popups show a curated, formatted set of fields with the title first?

name: Linked brushing across map, chart and table
keywords: linked; brushing; selection; chart; table; sync; shared state; highlight color
do: Keep one shared selection state and one highlight color across map, chart and table.
dont: Do not let each widget keep its own selection.
why: Linked views let users spot patterns across representations.
checklist: Do map, chart and table share one selection state and highlight color?

name: flyTo and reduced motion
keywords: flyTo; animation; speed; curve; maxDuration; reduced motion; camera
do: Use flyTo defaults speed 1.2 and curve 1.42; set maxDuration; honor prefers-reduced-motion (the animation becomes a jump unless essential:true).
dont: Do not fly across the globe for a nearby selection or ignore reduced-motion.
why: Long camera animations disorient users and trigger motion sickness.

name: Locator results list
keywords: locator; results list; distance; hours; directions; markers; sync; store finder
do: List name, distance, hours and Directions per result, and keep the list in sync with the markers.
dont: Do not show markers without a list or a list that ignores the map extent.
why: Locator users compare options by distance and hours.

name: URL holds the view state
keywords: url; hash; deep link; share; state; permalink; view state
do: Store center, zoom, layers, time and selection in the URL.
dont: Do not make views unshareable or lose state on reload.
why: Shareable URLs support collaboration and the back button.

name: Show active filters
keywords: filter; chips; active filters; N of M; features shown; reset; count
do: Show filter chips and an 'N of M features shown' count with a clear-all action.
dont: Do not filter silently.
why: Users who forget an active filter think data is missing.
checklist: Are active filters shown as chips with an 'N of M features' count?

name: Compare modes
keywords: compare; swipe; before after; opacity fade; spy lens; change detection; slider
do: Offer swipe as the default compare mode, with opacity fade and spy lens as alternatives.
dont: Do not make users toggle layers on and off to compare dates.
why: Side-by-side modes make change visible.
checklist: Is there a swipe, fade or lens compare mode for before and after imagery?

name: Label the A/B dates on both halves
keywords: dates; label; before after; a b; swipe; both sides; timestamp
do: Label the date (and source) on both halves of a compare view.
dont: Do not leave the two sides unlabeled.
why: Without dates the viewer cannot tell which side is before.
checklist: Are the dates labeled on both sides of the compare view?

name: Swipe controls
keywords: swipe; swap; orientation; legend; handle; direction
do: Add swap and orientation controls; note that a legend may not apply to both sides.
dont: Do not assume one legend fits both sides.
why: Different layers or dates may have different symbology.

name: Time slider
keywords: time slider; stops; playback; window; loop; rate; pause; animation
do: Use explicit stops, instant or window mode, a configurable rate and loop; pause playback while the view is loading.
dont: Do not advance frames while tiles are still loading.
why: Skipped frames hide data.

name: Timelapse export
keywords: timelapse; export; gif; mp4; fps; frequency; range
do: Choose range, fps and frequency; export GIF or MP4; state which visualization is animated.
dont: Do not export an animation without date range and visualization labels.
why: Exports are shared without the UI context.

name: Cloud cover filter
keywords: cloud cover; cloud filter; max cloud; percent; sentinel; scene; 30%
do: Provide a cloud cover filter with a default maximum of 30% (as in Copernicus Browser for Sentinel-2 L2A) and make it adjustable.
dont: Do not show all scenes regardless of cloud cover.
why: Cloudy scenes are unusable for most optical analysis.
checklist: Is there an adjustable cloud cover filter, defaulting to about 30%?

name: Disclose that cloud % is per scene
keywords: cloud percent; per scene; per aoi; disclosure; aoi cloud; metadata
do: State that cloud percent is per scene, not per AOI, or compute it for the AOI.
dont: Do not present scene cloud percent as AOI cloud percent.
why: A clear scene can have a cloud over the AOI and the reverse.
checklist: Does the UI say cloud % is per scene (or compute it per AOI)?

name: Date picker marks acquisition dates
keywords: date picker; acquisition dates; calendar; available dates; grey out; no data
do: Mark acquisition dates in the date picker and grey out dates with no data.
dont: Do not let users pick dates that return nothing.
why: Empty results waste time.

name: Time series flags cloudy observations
keywords: time series; cloudy; flag; remove; ndvi chart; noise; observations
do: Flag or remove cloudy observations in time series charts.
dont: Do not plot cloud-contaminated values as real signal.
why: Cloud-affected points create false dips and spikes.
checklist: Are cloudy observations flagged or removed from time series?

name: A few KPIs with reference and units
keywords: kpi; indicator; reference value; units; target; comparison; headline
do: Show a few KPIs, each with a reference value (previous period or target) and units.
dont: Do not show bare numbers without context.
why: A number only has meaning against a baseline.
checklist: Does every KPI have units and a reference value?

name: Show data freshness
keywords: freshness; last updated; refresh; timestamp; stale; data age; indicator
do: Show a 'last updated' timestamp and align the refresh interval with the layer refresh.
dont: Do not leave users guessing how current the data is.
why: Indicators that do not reflect layer refresh show stale numbers as current.
checklist: Is a last-updated time shown and refresh aligned with the layer?

name: Pre-aggregate at the source
keywords: aggregate; pre-aggregated; fields; load; statistics; performance; dashboard
do: Pre-aggregate at the source and load only the needed fields.
dont: Do not pull all features to the client to compute totals.
why: Large downloads slow every widget.
checklist: Are statistics pre-aggregated and only needed fields loaded?

name: Prefer attribute filters over extent filters
keywords: attribute filter; extent filter; high traffic; scalable; dashboard; query
do: Prefer attribute filters over map-extent filters on high-traffic dashboards.
dont: Do not rerun every widget query on every pan.
why: Extent filters create many unique queries that defeat caching.

name: Limit relative-date filters at scale
keywords: relative date; filter; scalable; cache; today; last 7 days
do: Limit relative-date filters (last 7 days) on large, high-traffic dashboards.
dont: Do not make every widget use a unique relative date.
why: Constantly changing queries cannot be cached.

name: One categorical palette for map and charts
keywords: palette; categorical; shared colors; chart; map; consistent; legend
do: Use one categorical palette shared by the map and charts.
dont: Do not color the same category differently in two widgets.
why: Consistent color lets users link map and chart without reading legends.
checklist: Do map and charts share one categorical palette?

name: Label chart series directly
keywords: direct labels; series; chart; legend; labeling; line chart
do: Label chart series directly instead of through a separate legend.
dont: Do not make users match colors between a distant legend and lines.
why: Direct labels reduce eye travel.

name: Encode uncertainty
keywords: uncertainty; vsup; confidence; bivariate; error; reliability; margin
do: Encode uncertainty with a VSUP or a separate confidence channel.
dont: Do not show estimates with high error at the same visual certainty as reliable ones.
why: Readers over-trust precise-looking colors.
checklist: Is uncertainty encoded (VSUP or a confidence channel)?

name: Alert list linked to map
keywords: alert list; severity; sort; zoom; highlight; scroll; selected; incident
do: Sort alerts by severity and time; clicking an alert zooms and highlights it; the list scrolls to the item selected on the map.
dont: Do not make the list and the map independent.
why: Operators need to move between where and what quickly.
checklist: Does the alert list sort by severity/time and sync with map selection both ways?

name: Source and date per layer, readable without hover
keywords: provenance; source; acquisition date; capture date; layer list; legend; lineage; truncated; tooltip
do: Show each layer's source and acquisition date (or "date not published") in the legend or layer list, readable without hover.
dont: Do not put source and date in a truncated line or only in a hover tooltip.
why: Users judge trust and currency per layer, and a tooltip is not reachable by touch or keyboard.
checklist: Does every layer show its source and acquisition date without hover?

name: Name composites by purpose
keywords: composite; true color; false color; band; name; ndvi; preset; label
do: Name composites by purpose: 'True color', 'False color (vegetation)', 'NDVI'.
dont: Never show bare band strings such as B08,B04,B03.
why: Users who are not remote-sensing experts cannot read band combinations.
checklist: Are composites named by purpose instead of bare band codes?

name: S2 true color is B04/B03/B02
keywords: sentinel-2; true color; b04; b03; b02; false color; bands
do: Label Sentinel-2 B04/B03/B02 as true color and every other combination as false color.
dont: Do not call a false-color composite natural or true color.
why: Users misread vegetation and water colors otherwise.

name: Fixed index domains
keywords: ndvi; ndwi; index; domain; stretch; -1 to 1; legend ticks; auto-stretch
do: Use a fixed domain (-1 to 1 for NDVI and NDWI) with a ticked legend.
dont: Never auto-stretch an index per scene.
why: Per-scene stretching makes scenes incomparable and changes meaning.
checklist: Do index layers use a fixed domain with a ticked legend?

name: SAR in dB
keywords: sar; sentinel-1; db; vv; vh; backscatter; water dark; urban bright
do: Display SAR in dB and use a VV, VH, VV-VH composite; explain that water is dark and urban is bright.
dont: Do not show raw linear SAR values without explanation.
why: SAR is unintuitive for non-specialists.

name: Scene cards
keywords: scene; card; thumbnail; date; coverage; resolution; sensor; cloud; search results
do: Show a scene card with thumbnail, date, AOI coverage %, resolution, sensor and cloud %.
dont: Do not list scenes by ID only.
why: Users pick scenes on these facts.
checklist: Do scene cards show thumbnail, date, AOI coverage, resolution, sensor and cloud %?

name: AOI coverage filter
keywords: aoi coverage; footprint; hover; filter; overlap; scene footprint
do: Provide an AOI coverage filter and show the footprint on hover.
dont: Do not return scenes that barely overlap the AOI without saying so.
why: Partial coverage causes mosaic gaps.

name: Mute imagery under detections
keywords: detections; mute imagery; highlight effect; dim; desaturate; mask
do: Dim or desaturate imagery under detections or highlighted areas.
dont: Do not draw bright overlays on bright imagery.
why: Muting raises contrast for the highlighted features.

name: Show AI detection confidence
keywords: confidence; detection; ai; threshold; model score; opacity; slider
do: Show confidence in the popup and the list, add a threshold slider and encode it visually (opacity or dash).
dont: Do not show model detections as certain.
why: Users must be able to trade recall against precision.
checklist: Is detection confidence shown, filterable by threshold, and visually encoded?

name: State the AIS match gate and time offset
keywords: ais; sar; match; gate; radius; time offset; interpolate; tolerance; dark vessel; unmatched
do: Interpolate AIS to the SAR acquisition time, and state the match radius and time tolerance (and the offset per pair) in the UI.
dont: Do not label a detection "no AIS match" without showing the gate that was used.
why: SAR and AIS are never simultaneous, and the unmatched count depends on the chosen gate.
checklist: Does the UI state the AIS match radius and time tolerance, and the offset to the SAR time?

name: Large data goes to vector tiles
keywords: large geojson; slow; vector tiles; pmtiles; mvt; mts; performance; tiling
do: Move large datasets to vector tiles (Mapbox Tiling Service, PMTiles or MVT). Docs suggest extra techniques above about 500,000 data points.
dont: Do not load huge GeoJSON files into the browser.
why: The browser parses and re-tiles all of it on the main thread.
checklist: Are large datasets served as vector tiles instead of one big GeoJSON?

name: Slim GeoJSON
keywords: geojson; decimals; precision; properties; maxzoom; url; slim; size
do: Keep at most 6 coordinate decimals, only the needed properties, load by URL and set source maxzoom below 18 (default 18; the docs suggest 12 for most point sources).
dont: Do not inline large GeoJSON objects or carry unused properties.
why: Smaller files parse faster and cost less bandwidth.
checklist: Is GeoJSON trimmed (6 decimals, needed properties only, loaded by URL, maxzoom set)?

name: Clustering with supercluster
keywords: supercluster; cluster; dom markers; markers; points; thousands
do: Use supercluster for client-side clustering and render points as layers.
dont: Do not create per-point DOM markers beyond a few hundred points.
why: DOM markers are expensive; layers are GPU drawn.
checklist: Are points above a few hundred rendered as layers (clustered), not DOM markers?

name: Feedback by response time
keywords: loading; spinner; progress; response time; skeleton; feedback; indicator; wait
do: Under 0.1 s show nothing; around 1 s still no indicator (wait about 1 s before showing one); 2 to 10 s a spinner or skeleton; over 10 s a percent-done bar.
dont: Do not flash a spinner for fast responses.
why: Indicators that flash are noisier than the delay.

name: Skeletons for panels, thin bar for the map
keywords: skeleton; loading; panel; thin bar; fade in; placeholder; map loading
do: Use skeletons for panels with known layout (about 3 s or less) and a thin bar or fade-in for the map.
dont: Do not blank the map with a full-screen spinner.
why: A placeholder preserves layout and perceived speed.

name: Per-layer error state with retry
keywords: error; retry; failed layer; fallback; network; per layer; message
do: Show an error state with retry on the failing layer; other layers keep working.
dont: Do not fail the entire map for one layer.
why: A single bad service should not break a dashboard.
checklist: Does each layer show its own error state with retry, leaving others working?

name: Scale-dependent rendering and simplification
keywords: simplify; generalize; scale dependent; tolerance; detail; geometry
do: Simplify geometry and render features dependent on scale.
dont: Do not send full-resolution geometry to a small-scale view.
why: Detail beyond the pixel grid costs without value.

name: Text alternative
keywords: alt text; text alternative; summary; table; screen reader; wcag 1.1.1; map description
do: Provide a summary and a feature table or list as a text alternative for the map (WCAG 1.1.1).
dont: Do not leave the map as an unlabeled canvas.
why: Screen reader users cannot see the canvas.
checklist: Is there a text summary and feature table/list for the map content?
code_good:
3 districts flooded.

...

name: Keyboard-operable map and features
keywords: keyboard; arrow keys; zoom; enter; operable; focus; map keyboard
do: Support arrow keys to pan, +/- to zoom and Enter to open features.
dont: Do not make mouse use mandatory.
why: Keyboard-only users cannot otherwise use the map.
checklist: Can the map and features be operated with the keyboard alone?

name: No keyboard trap; skip link
keywords: keyboard trap; skip link; focus; tab; escape; map; bypass
do: Never trap keyboard focus in the map and add a skip link before it.
dont: Do not swallow Tab or Escape inside the map.
why: Users must be able to leave the map with the keyboard.
checklist: Can keyboard users tab out of the map, with a skip link before it?
code_good: Skip map

name: Visible focus and logical order
keywords: focus; visible focus; tab order; logical; skip link; search; controls
do: Keep visible focus and a logical order: skip link, search, controls, map, panels.
dont: Do not remove the focus outline.
why: Users must see where they are.
checklist: Is focus visible and the tab order logical?

name: Non-drag alternatives
keywords: drag alternative; swipe; time slider; wcag 2.5.7; single pointer; buttons; step
do: Provide a non-drag alternative for pan, swipe and the time slider (WCAG 2.5.7).
dont: Do not make dragging the only interaction.
why: People with motor impairments cannot drag.
checklist: Do pan, swipe and the time slider each have a non-drag alternative?

name: Contrast
keywords: contrast; 4.5:1; 3:1; text; symbols; outlines; wcag 1.4.11; ratio
do: Text at least 4.5:1; symbols and outlines at least 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11).
dont: Do not rely on pale outlines on a busy basemap.
why: Low contrast is unreadable for many users.
checklist: Do text (4.5:1) and symbols or outlines (3:1) meet contrast minimums?

name: Never use color alone
keywords: color alone; icon; pattern; label; wcag 1.4.1; shape; redundant
do: Add an icon, pattern or label in addition to color (WCAG 1.4.1).
dont: Do not encode status or category in color only.
why: Color-vision deficiency and grayscale printing lose it.
checklist: Is every color-coded meaning also shown by icon, pattern or label?

name: Accessible names on markers
keywords: aria label; marker; accessible name; decorative; inert; role; alt
do: Give interactive markers an accessible name; make decorative maps inert.
dont: Do not leave focusable unnamed markers.
why: Screen readers announce unnamed controls as 'button'.
checklist: Do markers have accessible names, and are decorative maps inert?

name: prefers-reduced-motion
keywords: reduced motion; animation; autoplay; pulsing; flyTo; motion; vestibular
do: Honor prefers-reduced-motion by disabling flyTo, autoplay and pulsing.
dont: Do not autoplay or pulse regardless of the setting.
why: Motion can trigger vestibular symptoms.

name: Focus management for popups
keywords: popup; focus; announce; return focus; dialog; aria-live; close
do: Move focus into the popup, announce it and return focus on close.
dont: Do not open popups without moving focus.
why: Keyboard and screen reader users lose context otherwise.
checklist: Does a popup take focus when it opens and return it on close?
code_bad: new mapboxgl.Popup().setHTML(h).addTo(map); // focus stays on the map

name: Touch targets
keywords: touch target; 44px; 24px; mobile; tap; size; wcag 2.5.8
do: Make touch targets at least 44 px on mobile (WCAG 2.5.8 sets 24 by 24 CSS px as the minimum at AA).
dont: Do not use tiny map controls on touch devices.
why: Fingers are imprecise.
